title: Pointwise strict-local derived-unit fibre comparison
statement: Let f:X\to S and a geometric point x of X [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-geometric-point] determine strict henselizations B=X_(x), A=S_(fx) and their canonical map h:B\to A [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit, lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. Let K be separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed], u:Spec K\to A, t=(A\to S)u, E=A\times_S Spec K, Y=B\times_S Spec K, p:Y\to E, and a:E\to Spec K [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let F be any abelian etale sheaf on Spec K and q\geq0 [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Let M be H^q of the derived unit a^{-1}F[0]\to Rp_*p^{-1}a^{-1}F[0] [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-exact-conservative]. For every point z of E there is a lift v:Spec K\to A of t such that the geometric point \bar z given by its algebraic-closure residue field satisfies pr_A\bar z=v a\bar z, and the stalk of M at \bar z is invertible exactly when H^q(Spec K,F)\to H^q(B\times_(A,v)Spec K,F) is bijective [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Conversely, every lift v of t admits such a point z with the same projection equality and the same equivalence.

proof.text: Use the proved affineness and ind-etale coordinate-ring theorems on E. Its canonical K-algebra structure is the one induced by a:E to Spec K. Factor B to S through the same affine chart by its closed-point property. A fibre product of the resulting affine schemes over that chart makes Y affine.

For every prime $z$ of $C$, its pullback to each finite product $K^{I_i}$ selects a unique factor, by the finite-product spectrum statement. If $c\in C$ is represented by $(\lambda_j)_j\in K^{I_i}$ and the selected factor is $j_0$, the corresponding idempotent $e_{j_0}$ is outside $z$ and kills $c-\lambda_{j_0}$. Consequently every element of $C_z$ is a scalar in $K$: denominators outside $z$ have nonzero selected scalar and can be inverted in $K$. The structural map $K\to C_z$ is injective since it is a map from a field to a nonzero local ring. Thus $C_z\cong K$, compatibly with the structural maps. Every prime is therefore maximal, and the zero-dimensional spectrum theorem makes $|E|$ profinite. Points of $E$ are exactly $K$-morphisms $T\to E$, equivalently lifts $v:T\to A$ of $t$, since each residue field is canonically $K$. The given $u$ supplies one such point, so $E$ is nonempty. Finite stages can have unused factors; no surjectivity of their transition maps is assumed.

proof.text: Using the ind-etale coordinate ring, a pointed affine etale neighbourhood has a K-valued section at the marked prime. Spread its finitely many generators and relations to a principal neighbourhood, then choose a clopen refinement using the profinite basis. Given two pointed maps, shrink to an affine target chart; their finitely many generator differences vanish in the local ring and are annihilated after a further principal shrinking. A smaller clopen equalizes them. Thus pointed clopens form a cofinal system, including equalization. Their ring colimit is the local ring K: every fraction is defined on a smaller clopen and a section with zero germ vanishes after a smaller clopen shrinking. This identifies the strict localization with Spec K. The same argument on Spec K identifies its sheaf sections with every geometric stalk.

source.place: Tags 09AY and 03PN; corrected Tag 0EZV proof after the finite-product presentation, clopen cofinality and stalk detection paragraphs

proof.text: Fix $z\in E$, equivalently a lift $v:T\to A$, and a geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to E$ over it as in step 3. Cofinality of the clopen neighbourhoods from step 3 identifies the strict localization of $E$ at $\bar z$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_z=T$: the clopen-idempotent theorem writes each affine clopen as $D(e)=\operatorname{Spec}C_e$. The ring colimit of these $C_e$ is the ordinary localization $C_z$: its natural map to $C_z$ is surjective since every fraction $c/s$ is defined on a clopen inside $D(s)$, and is injective since a section zero in $C_z$ is annihilated by some element outside $z$ and becomes zero on a smaller clopen inside its basic open. Thus the ring colimit over pointed etale neighbourhoods is $C_z$, since every denominator outside $z$ is inverted on a clopen neighbourhood contained in its basic open, and step 2 identifies that localization with $K$. The unrestricted strict-henselization stalk theorem applies to the affine, hence qcqs, morphism $p$ and the abelian sheaf $p^{-1}G$. It gives $(R^qp_*p^{-1}G)_{\bar z}\cong H^q(Y\times_E T,F)$. Fibre-product associativity, checked by their projections, identifies $Y\times_E T$ with $B\times_{A,v}T$. By the inverse-image stalk-and-germ theorem for $a:E\to T$, the source stalk $G_{\bar z}$ is $F_{a\bar z}$; step 3 on $T$ identifies this canonically with $F(T)=H^0(T,F)$. For $q=0$ the stalk of $\eta$ is the section-pullback unit $H^0(T,F)\to H^0(B\times_{A,v}T,F)$: a clopen representative of a germ restricts along the section in step 3, and its unit image restricts along the base-changed section, giving exactly the fibre pullback. For $q>0$, $H^q(T,F)=0$ by step 4, so the fibre comparison is invertible exactly when this higher-direct-image stalk vanishes. The clopen system is independent of the chosen $\Omega$ by step 3, so these identifications hold for every geometric point over $z$. This identifies the actual canonical maps, not just abstract groups.

proof.text: The residue-field identification K = kappa(z) identifies sections Spec K to E with all its points. Apply it to a given point, and conversely take the point of any given section. The pullback universal property identifies such sections with lifts to A of the fixed t, and the projection equations give the asserted equality after the algebraic-closure point.

theorem strictLocalFibre_unit_stalks
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X) (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsSepClosed K]
    (u : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme (x ≫ f))
    (F : Sheaf (Spec (.of K)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (q : ℕ) :
    let t := u ≫ Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap (x ≫ f)
    let p := pullback.map
      (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap x ≫ f) t
      (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap (x ≫ f)) t
      (Scheme.strictHenselizationMap f x) (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _)
      (by simpa using (Scheme.strictHenselizationMap_over f x).symm) (by simp)
    let a := pullback.snd (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap (x ≫ f)) t
    let E := pullback (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap (x ≫ f)) t
    let M := derivedPullbackUnitHomology p
      ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} a).obj F) q
    (∀ z : E, ∃ v : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme (x ≫ f),
      v ≫ Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap (x ≫ f) = t ∧
      E.algClosurePoint z ≫
          pullback.fst (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap (x ≫ f)) t =
        (E.algClosurePoint z ≫ a) ≫ v ∧
      (IsIso ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale (E.algClosurePoint z)).sheafFiber.map M) ↔
        Function.Bijective (cohomologyMap
          (pullback.snd (Scheme.strictHenselizationMap f x) v) F q))) ∧
    (∀ (v : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme (x ≫ f)),
      v ≫ Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap (x ≫ f) = t →
      ∃ z : E,
        E.algClosurePoint z ≫
            pullback.fst (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap (x ≫ f)) t =
          (E.algClosurePoint z ≫ a) ≫ v ∧
        (IsIso ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale (E.algClosurePoint z)).sheafFiber.map M) ↔
          Function.Bijective (cohomologyMap
            (pullback.snd (Scheme.strictHenselizationMap f x) v) F q)))
